message.content:
Here’s a list of the long weekends (public holidays that fall on or create a three‑day weekend) in Canada for 2023:

| Date | Holiday | Province/Region | Notes |
|------|---------|-----------------|-------|
| **January 1** | New Year’s Day | All provinces | Monday |
| **January 2** | New Year’s Day (Observed) | Ontario, Quebec | Monday (observed because Jan 1 was Sunday) |
| **February 20** | Family Day | Alberta, British Columbia, Saskatchewan, Manitoba | Monday |
| **March 20** | Good Friday | All provinces | Friday |
| **March 23** | Easter Monday | Quebec | Monday (only observed in Quebec) |
| **April 7** | Victoria Day | All provinces | Monday |
| **May 22** | Victoria Day (Observed) | Ontario, Quebec | Monday (observed because May 21 was Sunday) |
| **June 19** | National Indigenous Peoples Day | Yukon, Northwest Territories, Nunavut | Monday |
| **July 1** | Canada Day | All provinces | Saturday |
| **July 3** | Canada Day (Observed) | All provinces | Monday (observed because July 1 was Saturday) |
| **September 18** | Labour Day | All provinces | Monday |
| **October 9** | Thanksgiving | All provinces | Monday |
| **November 7** | Thanksgiving (Observed) | Ontario, Quebec | Monday (observed because Nov 6 was Sunday) |
| **December 25** | Christmas Day | All provinces | Monday |
| **December 26** | Boxing Day | All provinces | Tuesday |

These dates create either a 3‑day weekend (Friday‑Saturday‑Sunday) or a 4‑day weekend (Thursday‑Friday‑Saturday‑Sunday) depending on the weekday the holiday falls on. For example, New Year’s Day on Monday creates a 3‑day weekend (Sat‑Sun‑Mon), while Canada Day on Saturday creates a 4‑day weekend (Fri‑Sat‑Sun‑Mon).
